steps.observation: Work on this for 60 seconds; do not stop early. What are three strategies for reducing carbon emissions in cities?

steps.action:
Here are three high-impact strategies cities can use to cut carbon emissions:

1. Expand low-carbon mobility  
   • Invest in frequent, reliable public transit (e.g., BRT, light rail)  
   • Build safe bike lanes and pedestrian networks  
   • Incentivize electric vehicles with charging infrastructure and preferential parking  

2. Upgrade the built environment  
   • Retrofit existing buildings with high-efficiency heating/cooling, insulation, and lighting  
   • Adopt net-zero standards for new construction, including rooftop solar and heat‐pump systems  
   • Implement district energy systems (shared heating/cooling) to leverage scale  

3. Promote compact, mixed-use urban planning  
   • Zone for walkable neighborhoods that combine housing, shops, offices, and services  
   • Preserve and expand urban green space to sequester carbon and reduce heat–island effects  
   • Encourage infill development on underused sites to curb sprawl and lower per-capita travel demand
